Scaling Laws, Carefully

Kaplan and Chinchilla compare how model size, dataset size, and training compute should grow. This introductory paragraph provides enough readable article context for smart translation.

The most influential and, in hindsight, most contested conclusion was the compute-optimal allocation. Kaplan et al. found Noptproportional toC0.73 and concluded that model size should grow faster than dataset size. Concretely, for a 10x increase in compute they suggested scaling the model size by ~5.5x but the training tokens by only ~1.8x. The Chinchilla paper would later overturn this recommendation, arguing that it leaves large models badly undertrained.

Another useful analysis approximates the number of training FLOPs needed from model size and dataset size. Each multiply-add is counted as about two floating-point operations.
